CSS 551 · Advanced 3D Computer Graphics

HW6 · A Whitted ray tracer and the Cornell box

Out Thursday November 12 · due Wednesday November 18, 11:59 PM on Canvas · 2.5 % of the course grade · Unity or WebGL · hub · schedule · syllabus · all homework
Read before this homework: Ray Tracing §1, the ray through a pixel · §2, sphere and triangle · §4, Whitted ray tracing · Light Transport and PBR (the bridge lecture)

What you build

A ray tracer that writes pixels: the primary ray through a pixel, the two intersections every scene needs, the reflection, and a trace that adds a shadow ray and one mirror bounce. The scene is a closed Cornell box, 96 × 72, lit directly by one point light, with a diffuse sphere and a mirror sphere. Four pixels are checked: a lit floor, a shadowed floor, the red wall seen in the mirror, and the red wall.

JavaScriptC#What it computes
cameraRayCameraRayThe unit ray through the center of pixel (px, py), top-left origin: screen x in [−1, 1] × tan(fov/2) × aspect, screen y × tan(fov/2), d = normalize(sx u + sy v − w).
hitSphereHitSphereThe smallest t > 10−6 of the quadratic; null (C#: −1) on a miss.
hitTriangleHitTriangleMöller–Trumbore: (t, u, v) with u weighting b and v weighting c; null (C#: false) on a miss, |det| < 10−12, or t ≤ 10−6.
reflectReflectd − 2 (d · n) n.
traceTraceMiss: black. P = hit + 10−4 N. Mirror: black at depth ≥ maxDepth, else mirror × trace of the reflected ray. Diffuse: albedo × (ka + (1 − ka) V max(0, N·L)), V = 0 when a hit lies closer than the light along P → light.
  • intersect (the closest hit over the scene, normal flipped to face the ray) and render are given and use your functions.
  • ka = 0.1, maxDepth = 3, light (0, 1.9, 0); the box spans x ∈ [−1, 1], y ∈ [0, 2], z ∈ [−1, 3]; the camera is at (0, 1, 2.8) looking at (0, 1, 0), fov 40°.

Implement and replace

Build each function from primitives (dot, cross, normalize, length, component access, sqrt, tan.) and use the engine's own helper, where one exists, only to check your result. These are off limits in your submission:

TrackOff limits
WebGL (JavaScript)THREE.Raycaster; Ray.intersectSphere, intersectTriangle, intersectBox; Vector3.reflect; anything that renders the scene for you.
Unity (C#)Physics.Raycast and every collider; Ray, Plane and Bounds helpers; Vector3.Reflect; Camera.ScreenPointToRay, ViewportPointToRay. The image is a Texture2D written in C#.

Getting started

WebGL track.
  1. Download the course site: its repository (Code, then Download ZIP), or git clone it.
  2. From the site's root folder run python3 -m http.server 8000 and open http://localhost:8000/homework/run.html?hw=hw06.
  3. Edit lib/skeletons/hw06.js, the only file you change, and reload: the Checks table under the scene compares your numbers with the ones below.

The unfilled skeleton runs on this site too, so you can see the page before you start.

Unity track.
  1. In Unity Hub, create a new project with the 3D (Built-In Render Pipeline) template in editor 6000.3.11f1.
  2. From the same download, copy the files in homework/hw06/unity/ into Assets/HW06/.
  3. Create an empty GameObject, add the Checks component (namespace CSS551.HW06), and press Play: the Console lists every check with your value and the expected one.
  4. Edit HW06.cs; the other files are given.

The Unity files compile against a stand-in for the UnityEngine API and pass their checks with the reference solution, but they are new this quarter and have not yet been opened in the Unity editor. If one does not compile in 6000.3.11f1, post the error on the Canvas board and use the WebGL track meanwhile.

Submitting and grading

  • WebGL: the one file hw06.js.
  • Unity: the project folder, zipped, without Library/, Temp/, Logs/ and obj/.

Grading runs your functions twice: on the published inputs above and on a second set of inputs that is not published. A check earns its points only when your value is within its tolerance on both, so the numbers have to come from the math. The score is the sum of the points earned, out of 100. A submission that does not load or compile earns no check points. Name any collaborators and tools in the submission comment.

Late tokens. You have two for the quarter. Declare one in the submission comment to extend this homework by 24 hours without penalty. Beyond tokens, late homework loses 10 % per day for up to three days.
Canvas governs the due date. HW6 of 8.
